# Objective

In Lab 4, you explored a prepared General Conference dataset. In this lab, you will work backward from raw files and build a reproducible process that turns imperfect data into a dataset ready for analysis.

You will inspect messy records, use regular expressions to standardize text, parse dates and runtimes, remove rows that are not talks, resolve duplicate speaker metadata, join tables, and write a script that recreates the processed dataset.

The goal is not to make the data look correct by editing the CSV manually. The goal is to make the cleaning decisions explicit in code so the same process can be run again.

## Before you begin

This lab uses two raw files in `data/raw/`:

- `talks_raw.csv`: talk-level information, including transcript text.
- `speaker_metadata_raw.csv`: speaker-level metadata intended to be joined to the talk records.

The files contain a small selection of realistic data-quality problems. Do not edit either CSV manually.

## Regex reminders

These examples illustrate useful patterns. Adapt them to the actual values in your data.

```python
# Match a prefix only at the start of a string.
r"^(By Elder|By President|By Sister|By Brother)\s+"

# Match one or more whitespace characters.
r"\s+"

# Split a URL before its query string.
r"\?.*$"
```
:::
